content: The memory extension stores NDJSON with atomic appends, repairs malformed non-empty lines during initialization, and exposes memory_repair for on-demand recovery.
Pi natively enables or disables installed package extensions via `pi config`, with global and project-local resource filters persisted in settings.json.
Shared pi-tools configuration lives in lib/pi-tools-config.ts with defaults < global < trusted-project precedence and is tested by `npm run test:config`.
The always-available `extensions/pi-tools-settings.ts` provides registry-driven `/pi-tools` UI and scoped status/get/set/enable/disable commands; saved edits reload Pi when the UI closes.
`npm run format` runs Prettier across the repository; Prettier is a devDependency.
Tool-call compression research is indexed in `research/index.md`, with prior-art and technique records in the repository-root `research/` directory.
Pi 0.82.1 truncates LLM `bash` output before `tool_result` to its last 2,000 lines or 50 KiB, exposing full raw output only through a temporary-file path on successful truncation.

extensions/tool-output-compression/ provides observe-default result profiles, exact reuse, session-scoped raw retrieval, and the /tool-output dashboard; its tests run through npm run test:compression.
Tool-output compression uses a private SQLite store with WAL, synchronous=FULL, 600-permission files, bounded busy retries, retention/quota controls, and session-scoped retrieve_tool_output chunks.
`/tool-output` reports potential savings in observe mode and actual applied exact-reuse savings in apply mode, while `/tool-output prune` and `vacuum` maintain the SQLite store.
The root package declares `"type": "module"`, so Node runs the TypeScript ESM tests without `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` reparsing warnings.

The registered Vitest output profile uses `profiles.test.vitest.mode`, defaults to observe, and strictly compacts only standalone successful file-level or test-level reporter output after durable raw storage.
The registered bash JSON/JSONL profile uses profiles.structured.json.mode, defaults to observe, lexically minifies complete or line-bounded embedded values, and uses session-scoped raw retrieval.
The registered search-records bash profile uses profiles.search.records.mode, defaults to observe, and reversibly groups certified rg/grep opaque prefix:<decimal>:suffix records with raw retrieval.
The code-search extension shell is in extensions/code-search/, registers shared mode/output/budget settings, and has dedicated npm run test:code-search lifecycle tests.

extensions/code-search/worker.ts owns trusted-project SQLite discovery, Tree-sitter symbol indexing, validation refresh, source-free queries, and the optional session watcher through a typed worker protocol.

extensions/code-search/metrics.ts provides a private WAL/FULL SQLite daily aggregate store for code-search mode/event counts, latency, result/emitted bytes, budget limits, freshness, and rolling retention without source, query, path, or per-call data.

Trusted non-off code-search sessions persist aggregate metrics in metrics.sqlite; `/code-search [prune]` renders/prunes these 90-day-configurable rows, and apply-mode tools record actual latency, result count, emitted bytes, budget pressure, and freshness.
The custom stats footer measures last and aggregate TPS from assistant message_start-to-message_end stream intervals using final usage.output, so tool execution time is excluded.

Trusted non-off code-search sessions persist aggregate metrics in Pi's global agent `code-search-metrics.sqlite`; `/code-search [prune]` renders/prunes these globally configured retention rows, and apply-mode tools record actual latency, result count, emitted bytes, budget pressure, and freshness.
Pi 0.83.0 includes an official `examples/extensions/subagent/` extension that runs isolated `pi --mode json -p --no-session` child processes with single, parallel, and chained delegation modes.

The subagents extension publishes enabled, maxConcurrentWorkers (integer, default 2), models.task, and models.research settings and resolves trusted-project launch policy before creating a worker session.

extensions/subagents/supervisor.ts manages injectable persistent SDK worker sessions with retry disabled, atomic manifests and terse journals in tmp/subagents, shared immediate-refusal concurrency, Git observation, and paused interrupted-work recovery.

Task workers use subagent_task_launch, subagent_task_follow_up, and subagent_task_report; each concluded run persists a structured report plus full final response under tmp/subagents/<id>/reports and injects one bounded handoff with a non-context timeline entry.

Task-worker controls are exposed through subagent_task_control: redirect steers a live worker, checkpoint persists bounded recovery metadata, pause aborts resumably, cancel disposes terminally, and explicit resume reopens the saved SDK session after interrupted work is recovered as paused.

Research jobs use subagent_research_launch/report/control with the research model, retain full reports and normalized cited source indexes under tmp/subagents, send one bounded cited handoff, and deliver only that synthesis to an explicitly linked live task worker.

Subagents delegationMode defaults to proactive and injects per-turn main-agent guidance to autonomously launch bounded useful workers; manual disables that guidance, and SDK worker sessions suppress subagent tools and guidance to prevent recursion.

The Subagent workstreams widget shows only starting/running/paused/blocked/needs-decision rows with the newest bounded journal activity and clears itself when no workstream needs attention; settled and cancelled work remains in transcript handoffs only.

browser_start in extensions/browser-tools/index.ts spawns a hard-coded macOS Brave path without an error listener, so an absent executable emits an unhandled ChildProcess ENOENT error that exits Node.

browser_start now uses extensions/browser-tools/brave-launch.ts to consume child-process launch errors, turn absent macOS Brave executables into tool errors, and avoid leaving tracked process state on failure.
memory_remember now carries typed canonical memory details for a TUI renderer that shows stored content while preserving the concise raw tool result and hidden project-memory injection.

Pi ExtensionAPI can block validated individual tool calls via `tool_call` returning `{ block, reason }`, but `before_agent_start`, `turn_end`, and `agent_end` expose no turn-cancellation or required-delegation hook.

Pi 0.84.0 sendMessage({deliverAs:"nextTurn"}) keeps a custom message only in AgentSession's in-memory pending queue until the next user prompt, so durable deferred subagent handoffs need separate persisted queue state.

Task and research completion currently call sendMessage with triggerTurn:true, which starts an idle parent agent turn or steers a busy one; Pi has no reliable reading/composer-focus hook and nextTurn delivery is in-memory only.

Custom Stats Footer's module-level ResponseTpsMeter is shared by same-cwd in-process SDK worker sessions due Pi's cached extension factory, so interleaved worker/main events can inflate TPS; mutable footer state must be per factory and headless workers skipped.

Subagent completions persist atomic records under tmp/subagents/completion-inbox and are queued as bounded nextTurn custom messages only after parent settlement, then acknowledged on matching message_end.

Pi 0.84 workstream widgets can animate with a component-owned interval and tui.requestRender while TuiMainScreen differentially redraws changed rows; extensions cannot mutate individual lines directly.

Subagents expose subagent_wait to snapshot selected or all live workers, return bounded terminal inbox handoffs, consume them to prevent deferred duplicate delivery, and leave workers/inbox untouched on cancellation.

Pi preserves the per-turn system prompt override through auto-compaction retries in the same agent run; before_agent_start re-runs on the next top-level prompt, while memory's session_compact handler reinjects its custom context only at that next start.
`/pi-tools` now uses a root navigator with write scope plus extension rows, opens per-extension SettingsList detail screens, retains root scope for detail writes, and returns detail Esc to the root.

The package `pi.extensions: ["./extensions"]` auto-loads direct `extensions/*.ts`, so `extensions/pi-tools-settings.test.ts` runs in every SDK worker, its top-level `initTheme()` resets the shared process-global theme to dark, and it must not remain in the runtime extension directory.
Pi 0.84 passes the active Agent run AbortSignal to every custom tool execution; steering queues input after tool completion and does not abort tools, while Agent.abort aborts that signal.

While main-session subagent_wait is active, interactive/RPC input now aborts the wait, preserves workers and inbox records, and replays captured text/images FIFO after agent settlement via pi.sendUserMessage.
Subagents expose outputTailLines as a non-negative integer setting defaulting to 0 for concise live thinking and tool lifecycle widget tails.

ResearchWorkstreamService writes normalized reports and citation source indexes under tmp/subagents/<workstream>/ after settlement, but its worker brief does not explicitly direct worker-created notes there.
